```{r}
#| label: load-data

# ── Helper: load all CSV/JSON exports from one run directory ────────────────
load_run_data <- function(dir_path, label) {
  dir_path <- normalizePath(dir_path, mustWork = TRUE)

  meta     <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(dir_path, "metadata.json"))
  df_obj   <- read.csv(file.path(dir_path, "objectives.csv"))

  norm_path <- file.path(dir_path, "objectives_normalized.csv")
  df_norm   <- if (file.exists(norm_path)) read.csv(norm_path) else NULL

  hv_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "hypervolume_evolution.csv")
  df_hv    <- if (file.exists(hv_path)) read.csv(hv_path) else NULL

  pop_path <- file.path(dir_path, "population_stats.csv")
  df_pop   <- if (file.exists(pop_path)) read.csv(pop_path) else NULL

  psel_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "pixel_selection.csv")
  df_psel    <- if (file.exists(psel_path)) read.csv(psel_path) else NULL

  elig_path  <- file.path(dir_path, "eligible_pixels.csv")
  df_elig    <- if (file.exists(elig_path)) read.csv(elig_path) else NULL

  obj_names     <- unlist(meta$objective_names)
  raster_shape  <- unlist(meta$raster_info$shape)   # c(nrows, ncols)

  # Objective normalisation scales (for annotation, not applied here)
  norm_scales <- tryCatch(
    unlist(meta$algorithm$objective_normalization$scales),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # Invert minimised objectives whose values are negative for easier interpretation.
  # Objectives containing "anomaly" or "connectivity_gain" were minimised and are
  # stored as negative; negate them so that larger = better throughout all downstream plots.
  invert_cols <- grep("anomaly|connectivity_gain", obj_names, value = TRUE)
  if (length(invert_cols) > 0) {
    df_obj[, invert_cols] <- -df_obj[, invert_cols]
    if (!is.null(df_norm)) df_norm[, intersect(invert_cols, names(df_norm))] <-
      -df_norm[, intersect(invert_cols, names(df_norm))]
  }

  list(
    label        = label,
    dir          = dir_path,
    meta         = meta,
    obj_names    = obj_names,
    n_obj        = length(obj_names),
    n_solutions  = meta$n_solutions,
    n_nondom     = meta$n_nondominated_solutions,
    raster_shape = raster_shape,
    norm_scales  = norm_scales,
    df_obj       = df_obj,
    df_norm      = df_norm,
    df_hv        = df_hv,
    df_pop       = df_pop,
    df_psel      = df_psel,
    df_elig      = df_elig
  )
}

run_a <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_A, LABEL_A)
run_b <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_B, LABEL_B)
run_c <- load_run_data(RUN_DIR_C, LABEL_C)
```

## Objective redundancy: full vs 2-objective models
```{r}
#| label: redundancy-2obj-config

# ── Configure the three 2-objective run directories ───────────────────────────
# Replace each PLACEHOLDER with the actual r_inputs/ export path.
RUN_2OBJ <- list(
  list(dir = "../r_inputs/abiotic_biotic",
       label = "abiotic + biotic", dropped = "cost"),
  list(dir = "../r_inputs/abiotic_cost",
       label = "abiotic + cost",   dropped = "biotic"),
  list(dir = "../r_inputs/biotic_cost",
       label = "biotic + cost",    dropped = "abiotic")
)

# Pixels with RFOP >= this threshold are treated as "high priority"
TOP_RFOP_PCT <- 50

# Load each reduced run — skip gracefully if the directory isn't ready yet
runs_2obj <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(RUN_2OBJ, function(r) {
  tryCatch(
    { rd <- load_run_data(r$dir, r$label); rd$dropped <- r$dropped; rd },
    error = function(e) {
      message(sprintf("[redundancy] Could not load '%s': %s", r$label, conditionMessage(e)))
      NULL
    }
  )
}))
```

```{r}
#| label: redundancy-2obj-helpers
#| include: false

# Per-pixel RFOP vector (%) across non-dominated solutions, named by pixel key.
.rfop_vector <- function(run) {
  if (is.null(run$df_psel) || is.null(run$df_obj)) return(NULL)
  nd_ids  <- run$df_obj$solution_id[run$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1]
  if (length(nd_ids) == 0) return(NULL)
  psel_nd <- dplyr::filter(run$df_psel, solution_id %in% nd_ids)
  has_xy  <- all(c("x", "y") %in% names(psel_nd))
  psel_nd <- dplyr::mutate(
    psel_nd,
    pkey = if (has_xy) paste(round(x, 1), round(y, 1), sep = "_")
           else        paste(pixel_row, pixel_col, sep = "_")
  )
  rfop <- psel_nd |>
    dplyr::count(pkey, name = "n_sel") |>
    dplyr::mutate(rfop_pct = 100 * n_sel / length(nd_ids))
  setNames(rfop$rfop_pct, rfop$pkey)
}

# Pixel keys where RFOP >= threshold
.top_pixels <- function(v, pct) names(v)[v >= pct]

# Jaccard similarity between two character vectors
.jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  if (length(a) == 0 && length(b) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
}

rfop_a <- .rfop_vector(run_a)
top_a  <- .top_pixels(rfop_a, TOP_RFOP_PCT)
```

#### Selected pixels / spatial pattern

Jaccard similarity between the set of pixels with RFOP ≥ `r TOP_RFOP_PCT`% in the full model and each reduced model. A high value means the dropped objective was not needed to identify the same high-priority locations.

```{r}
#| label: redundancy-jaccard
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 7

if (length(runs_2obj) == 0) {
  message("[redundancy] No 2-obj runs loaded — populate RUN_2OBJ directories above.")
} else {
  jac_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(runs_2obj, function(r2) {
    v2    <- .rfop_vector(r2)
    top_b <- .top_pixels(v2, TOP_RFOP_PCT)
    data.frame(
      model          = sprintf("%s\n(drops %s)", r2$label, r2$dropped),
      n_top_full     = length(top_a),
      n_top_reduced  = length(top_b),
      jaccard        = .jaccard(top_a, top_b)
    )
  }))

  jac_plot <- ggplot(jac_df, aes(x = jaccard, y = reorder(model, jaccard), fill = jaccard)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("J = %.3f  (full: %d px | reduced: %d px)", jaccard, n_top_full, n_top_reduced)),
      hjust = -0.05, size = 3.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#d73027", high = "#4dac26", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.3),
                       labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    labs(
      title    = sprintf("Jaccard similarity: top-%d%% RFOP pixels (full vs 2-obj)", TOP_RFOP_PCT),
      subtitle = "Higher = reduced model identifies the same high-priority pixels, implying the dropped objective is redundant",
      x = "Jaccard similarity", y = NULL
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: redundancy-rank-corr
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 7

if (length(runs_2obj) == 0 || is.null(rfop_a)) {
  message("[redundancy] No data available for rank correlation.")
} else {
  df_a <- data.frame(pkey = names(rfop_a), rfop_a = unname(rfop_a),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  rcor_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(runs_2obj, function(r2) {
    v2 <- .rfop_vector(r2)
    if (is.null(v2)) {
      print(sprintf("[redundancy] No RFOP vector for '%s' — pixel_selection.csv missing?", r2$label))
      return(data.frame(model = sprintf("%s\n(drops %s)", r2$label, r2$dropped),
                        rho = NA_real_, n_matched = 0L))
    }
    df_b   <- data.frame(pkey = names(v2), rfop_b = unname(v2),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    joined <- dplyr::full_join(df_a, df_b, by = "pkey")
    joined[is.na(joined$rfop_a), "rfop_a"] <- 0
    joined[is.na(joined$rfop_b), "rfop_b"] <- 0
    rho <- cor(joined$rfop_a, joined$rfop_b, method = "spearman")
    data.frame(
      model     = sprintf("%s\n(drops %s)", r2$label, r2$dropped),
      rho       = rho,
      n_matched = sum(joined$rfop_a > 0 & joined$rfop_b > 0)
    )
  }))

  
  rankcor_plot <- ggplot(rcor_df, aes(x = rho, y = reorder(model, ifelse(is.na(rho), -Inf, rho)), fill = rho)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = ifelse(is.na(rho), "no data",
                         sprintf("\u03c1 = %.3f  (%d shared px)", rho, n_matched))),
      hjust = -0.05, size = 3.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#d73027", high = "#4dac26",
                        limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey80") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    labs(
      title    = "Spearman rank correlation of RFOP maps (full vs 2-obj models)",
      subtitle = "Higher = pixel ranking preserved when objective is dropped, i.e. more redundant",
      x = "Spearman \u03c1", y = NULL
    )
}

jac_plot + rankcor_plot + plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

#### 3. Objective value distributions

Distribution of non-dominated objective values across the Pareto front, comparing the full model against each 2-objective reduced model. Only the objectives shared by both models are shown in each panel. If the two distributions are similar — same median and spread — the dropped objective was not competing against the others, consistent with redundancy: the algorithm was effectively already ignoring it. If the reduced model achieves clearly better values (a shifted distribution towards lower cost or higher anomaly improvement), the dropped objective was genuinely constraining the optimisation and is non-redundant — removing it allowed the algorithm to improve on the remaining objectives by no longer needing to make trade-offs against the dropped one.

```{r}
#| label: redundancy-obj-distributions
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 12

if (length(runs_2obj) == 0) {
  message("[redundancy] No 2-obj runs loaded — configure RUN_2OBJ above.")
} else {
  obj_dist_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(list(run_a), runs_2obj), function(r) {
    nd      <- r$df_obj[r$df_obj$is_nondominated == 1, , drop = FALSE]
    # shared = objectives present in both this run and the full model
    shared  <- intersect(obj_names, names(nd))
    if (length(shared) == 0) return(NULL)
    dropped_lbl <- if (!is.null(r$dropped)) sprintf("drops %s", r$dropped) else "full model"
    nd[, shared, drop = FALSE] |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::everything(),
                          names_to  = "objective",
                          values_to = "value") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        model   = r$label,
        dropped = dropped_lbl,
        is_full = r$label == run_a$label
      )
  }))

  obj_dist_df <- obj_dist_df |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      objective = gsub("_", " ", objective) |> tools::toTitleCase(),
      model     = factor(model, levels = c(run_a$label,
                                           sapply(runs_2obj, `[[`, "label")))
    )

  ggplot(obj_dist_df, aes(x = model, y = value, fill = model)) +
    geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.45, colour = NA, scale = "width") +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, colour = "grey30", fill = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~objective, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Model") +
    labs(
      title    = "Non-dominated objective value distributions: full vs 2-obj models",
      subtitle = "Each panel shows only the objectives shared between both compared models",
      x = NULL, y = "Objective value"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}
```

## Do trade-offs exist in space?

Pairwise spatial similarity (Jaccard index) between non-dominated solutions, plotted against Euclidean distance in normalised objective space.

Negative relationship = solutions with lower spatial overlap correspond to greater differences in objective performance, indicating that trade-offs in the Pareto set are driven by distinct spatial configurations.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6

```

## Spatial distribution of selected areas

Relative frequency of occurrence in the Pareto front (RFOP): how often each pixel appears across the non-dominated solutions. Coloured pixels were selected in ≥ 1 solution. Grey underlay indicates pixels that were eligible for selection but never selected in any non-dominated solution.

# Sensitivity

| Type | Sources of uncertainty | References |
|---|---|---|
| Epistemic uncertainties | Condition index/anomaly construction; Benchmark used for reference condition | Czúcz et al., 2021; Jepsen et al., 2024; Paper 1 |
| Exogenous uncertainties | LULC/Climate change scenarios; Disturbance regimes | Lempert |
| Policy levers | Area targets; Municipal burden sharing | Lempert |
| Model relationships | Objective functions; Restoration response (WP3) | Lempert, Lohmus |

